md: Happy is the man. This tells the merits of the man — it is said in his praise: this is the one who has not followed the counsel of the wicked. That is, his heart was not tempted to follow their counsel and act like them. And he guarded himself so carefully that he did not even stand on the path the sinners walk, fearing they would meet him and lure him to their counsel. Since this is so, he certainly never came to sit with them, so that their counsel would not take root in his heart and he would not follow it. So he set a fence around a fence.
Rather. Not only did he stop and keep away from the counsel of the wicked — he also did good: all his desire was in the teaching of the L-rd.
And in his teaching. At all times he thinks and reflects on what he himself found in his heart: reasons and adornments — “blossoms” — for the Torah.

He is like. And for this his reward is to be like a tree planted by water, which grows its fruit in its season, and even its leaves do not wither, because there is so much moisture. So too this man is rich in every good and lacks nothing. As if to say: from the reward one sees how upright his way is. “And whatever it produces” — that is, whatever is “planted” from him will succeed and be like him: the children of this man will be like him.
Not so. The wicked will not have such success — the very opposite: many troubles await the wicked again and again, like this chaff that the wind keeps blowing away, and it finds no rest.
Therefore. Since many troubles are in store for them, they will not stand when judgment comes — when their measure is full: then the troubles will come upon them one after another.
Nor will sinners. The word “not” at the start of the verse serves here too, as if to say: the sinners will not be in the assembly of the righteous — watched over by the L-rd like them.

For the L-rd knows. For the Omnipresent, blessed be He, pays attention and watches over the way of the righteous so that they do not stumble on it. But the way of the wicked will be lost to the L-rd’s watching — left to chance; so they too will not be in the assembly of the righteous.
Why do they assemble. That is, why do they need this — to gather and speak empty words that neither help nor do any good?
Take their stand. This goes back to “why” in the previous verse: why do the kings and the princes take their stand in one plot against the L-rd and against His anointed?
Let us break. And this is what they say in their plot: let us tear off the bonds of His yoke so as not to serve Him. It is a parable — the language of an ox pulling a yoke.
Shake off. This repeats the same idea in other words — for beauty of speech and to make it stronger.

He who is enthroned in heaven. As if to say: the L-rd is enthroned in heaven above; even a weak one, if he is above, counts as strong — all the more a strong one above. So surely He laughs at their plot and mocks them. The idea is repeated in other words.
Then. When they plot in secret and make their plan, He will speak, etc.
But I. And so He will say: it is I who made him king — how then can you stand against Me? As if to say: we will see whose word will stand, yours or Mine.

Let me tell. David said: I will tell what is written — that the L-rd said to me, “You are My son,” as it says, “Israel is My son, My firstborn” (Exodus 4:22–23), and the king counts as the whole people.
I have fathered you this day. That is, you are dear to Me like a son to his father on the day he is born.
Ask. So ask of Me, and I will grant your request.
You can smash them. You will break them as one breaks something with an iron rod.
So now. Since he has the L-rd’s promise for all this, be prudent, accept discipline, and do not speak like this.
Serve the L-rd. Accept the yoke of His kingship.
And rejoice. Then you will rejoice when trembling comes upon the rebels, for the trembling will not be upon you.
Pay homage in good faith. Long with a pure heart to accept His kingship — wholeheartedly, without deceit.
Lest He be angered. For otherwise the L-rd may grow angry with you.
And your way be doomed. That is, you will wander, not knowing which way to turn.
When it flares. When His anger flares, even a little — then your way will be lost.
Happy. This is the praise of those who take refuge in the L-rd: they understood by themselves how great is the L-rd’s power and the might of His arm, and so they take refuge in Him.
A psalm. He said this prayer in song.
Of David. It is David’s, for he composed it.
When he fled. Then he foresaw by Divine inspiration that he would return to his kingdom, and he said this prayer in song.
How many are my foes. Even my son has risen against me.
Many. Great men — such as Shimi, Doeg and Achitofel.
Of me. They say of me that never again will I have deliverance from the L-rd: once he has begun to fall, he will not rise again.
But You, O L-rd. But it is not so: You are a shield for me, You uphold my glory and lift my head, for I will return to my kingdom.
My voice. When I call to the L-rd with my voice, I know that He will answer me from His holy mountain — that is Zion, the place of His Shechinah.
Selah. He will answer me forever; that is, it will be a lasting redemption: I will never again be an exile and a fugitive.
I lie down. When I lie down and fall asleep from great sorrow.
And wake. That is, my sorrow passed when I remembered that the L-rd sustains me.
I have no fear. So I do not fear the great crowd with Absalom who have set out to fight me.
Rise, O L-rd. Since I trust in You, it is fitting that You rise to save me.

For You slap. You have always struck my enemies on the cheek — a blow of disgrace, as it says, “Let him offer his cheek to the smiter; let him be filled with disgrace” (Lamentations 3:30); a slap on the cheek counts as disgrace.
The teeth of the wicked. Who gnashed their teeth at me in their anger — You have always broken them; so now too, do not take Your hand away from me.

Deliverance is the L-rd’s. Deliverance is in the L-rd’s hand, and He can save me from them. And may Your blessing be upon Your people forever. That is: save me so that they cannot harm me, yet may Your blessing be upon them too, so that they are not struck down either. As if to say: I do not pray for their downfall, only for my deliverance.
For the leader. That is, this psalm of David was given to the Levite leader to perform with a melody in the Temple.
When I call. When I call to You, answer me.
O G-d, my vindicator. You are my G-d who does me justice: always, when I was in distress and in straits, You set me in a wide place; so now too, have mercy on me.

You men. You great men — how long will you turn my glory into shame? That is, instead of the honor due to me you disgrace me. As if to say: surely it is right for distinguished people to honor one who deserves honor. “Will you love illusions” goes back to “how long”: how long will you love to speak empty, false words without end?
Know. Take note: just as the L-rd set apart every faithful one to be His and His portion, so He set me apart as His portion, and He will hear when I call to Him — and you cannot prevail against Him.
Tremble. Fear the L-rd, and do not sin against me by telling lies about me.

Ponder, etc. When you are on your bed — a time when a person’s thoughts are free of worries — think in your hearts that falsehood is evil in the eyes of the Omnipresent, and fall silent forever from telling lies.

Offer sacrifices. Make your deeds righteous, and the L-rd will count it as sacrifices; then trust in Him, for there is hope. Why do you betray Him by flattering Shaul for the money you gain from him? Surely it is better to take refuge in the L-rd.
Many. I have seen many who long and say, “Who will show us good?” — that is, they crave great wealth.
Bestow. “Lift up the light of Your face upon us, O L-rd, to fulfill our desires.”
You put. But I am not like that: You, O L-rd, have put joy in my heart at my portion, more than those many rejoice when their grain and wine increase.

Safe and sound. Without fear I lie down and sleep at once — one right after the other. For one who worries and is afraid is robbed of sleep: such people cannot fall asleep as soon as they lie down. But I trust in the L-rd and am not afraid, so I lie down and sleep together, one right after the other.
For You, O L-rd. Who rules over all, and it is in Your hand to let me dwell securely, without fear.
Consider my utterance. For my prayer comes from the heart.
For I pray to You. And a king kindly turns his ear to his servant who trusts in him and asks him for his request.
At daybreak. Every morning hear my voice: as soon as morning comes I set my prayer before You and put no business of my own before it; so I hope that You will hear my voice.
For You are not, etc. And You will not give strength to the wicked who do me harm.
Evil cannot abide with You. Evil does not dwell near You. It is a figure of speech: evil is hateful to the Omnipresent.
Cannot endure. You do not want the wicked to stand before Your eyes.

You doom. I know that You will destroy the one who tells lies about me before Shaul. For the L-rd has always abhorred one who lies in wait for his fellow’s blood and speaks to him deceitfully as a friend; so too He will abhor and destroy the one who tells lies about me, for he speaks to me deceitfully, as if he were my friend.
Through Your abundant love. Because of the great kindness You will do me, I will come into Your house to bow down.
In awe of You. And not to show off before people.

Lead me along Your righteous path. Put it into my heart to walk in the way of righteousness. And because of these wicked ones who watch and wait for my downfall — so that they will not say “our hand is strong” — let Your way seem straight in my eyes, so that I do not stumble on it: then they surely cannot prevail against me.

For there is no sincerity on their lips. No one of them has truth in his mouth: they look like friends, but inside they are enemies. Deep in their hearts they plot ruin to break me; their throat is like an open grave, for they long to swallow me as a grave swallows the dead; and with their tongue they speak smooth words that do not come from the heart.

Condemn them. So condemn them in judgment, and let them fall low because of their evil plans; and as many as their crimes are, so drive them from one calamity to the next — for they rebelled against You, who had warned against this.
But let rejoice. But those who take refuge in You will rejoice forever, and You will shelter them from harm.
In You. In Your deliverance.
For You, etc. Rearrange the words of the verse: for You, O L-rd, will bless the righteous man.
Like a shield. As a shield surrounds the body, so You will surround him with favor.
Not in fury. The idea is repeated in other words.
Have mercy on me. So that You will no longer be angry with me: I am wretched as it is — that is enough.
Heal me. He added to his request and said: heal me from the blows that have passed over me since then, for my bones are terrified.

My whole being. Even my soul is terrified. If so — how long will I still be stricken and beaten? The punishment itself comes to open the ear to discipline, and I am already terrified and have accepted the discipline.
O L-rd, turn. So turn to bring my soul out of trouble, and save me for the sake of Your kindness — even if I have not yet been punished as my sin deserves.
For there is no praise of You among the dead. For if I die from this trouble, I will no longer mention Your name: who gives thanks in the grave? Only the living, the living thank You.
I am weary. I have grown tired and weary from sighing all the time.
I drench. I make my bed float in the water of my weeping, like something that floats on water.
In tears. With the tears of my eyes I melt and soak my couch. The idea is repeated in other words.
Wasted by vexation. My eyes are worn out from the enemy’s anger.
Worn out. Because of my troubles my eye has dimmed, as if it had aged. So all the troubles that have already passed over me are enough.
Away from me. Go away from me, for from now on you cannot prevail against me — my prayer has been accepted.
Heeds, etc. The idea is repeated in other words.
Will be frustrated. When they see my success.
And stricken with terror. Like a person amazed and bewildered at seeing something he thought impossible.

They will turn back. Then they will turn from their evil and seek peace with me, and at that very moment they will be ashamed, not later: for I will forgive them what they did to me, and it will no longer be remembered to their shame.
Shiggaion of David. With this he prayed about his error (shegiah) — that he cut off the corner of Shaul’s robe.
Cush, a Benjaminite. This is Shaul, who came from Binyamin. He is called Cush because he was different in his deeds — for the better — as a Cushite is different in his skin.
Lest they tear. If You do not save me, the enemy will overpower me and tear me apart like a lion.
Rending. He will break me, and I will find no one to save me, for all have risen against me.
If I have done. If — when I did this: cut off the corner of Shaul’s robe…
If my hands bear the guilt of wrongdoing. Did I do it to commit a wrong, to shame him, to make him stand in a torn robe like a lowly person?
If I have dealt. While Shaul was my friend, did I repay him evil for good, as he thought, that I was his enemy?

I who rescued. Even when he was my foe and pursued me for nothing, though I had done no violence, his life was still precious to me, and I saved him from death: I rescued him from my men, who wanted to kill him, as told in I Samuel. As if to say: this is why I cut his robe — to let him know that he was in my hands and I did not harm him.

Let the enemy pursue. As if to say: and if it is not as I say, let my punishment be that the enemy pursues me, urges others to pursue me, overtakes me and tramples me to the ground all the days of my life, and lays my honor low, to dwell forever in the dust.
Rise, O L-rd. That is: though I did not sin against Shaul, I ask nothing against him and his men. But rise, O L-rd, in Your anger, and be exalted by bringing fury upon my foes.

Bestir Yourself on my behalf. Arouse for me the mighty strength of the arm to overcome them and carry out on them the judgment You commanded and decreed for them — that is, let the judgment on them be carried out through me.
The assembly. And even if the assembly of the Philistines, Ammon and Moav surrounds You, turning to You to save them, return on high because of it, keep away from it and do not turn to it.
Judges the peoples. When You judge the peoples with fitting judgment, then judge me by my righteousness and blamelessness; that is, judge me by my good deeds, and withdraw Your hand from my sins.
Let come to an end, etc. May the evil the wicked do accuse them, to wipe them from the world; and establish the righteous, to stand firm on his base and foundation.
He who probes. For You, G-d, probe the heart and mind of the righteous and know that his heart is wholly with You.
The deliverer. Because He delivers the upright in heart.
Vindicates the righteous. He judges with righteous judgment and is angry every day with those who do Him wrong.
If one does not turn back. If the one who pursues the righteous does not turn from his way: he still whets his sword, bends his bow and aims it to shoot at the righteous.

Against himself he readies. His punishment will be that he readied these deadly weapons against himself: the arrows he made with his own hands, he truly makes against the pursuer — that is, against himself, for he will be killed by them.

He hatches evil. Like a woman: what gives her the pangs of birth is the very thing she conceived, and that is what she bears. So too these wicked men: they did not do their evil deeds by chance but planned them from the start, and by that very thing they will be repaid.
He has dug a pit. With this he explains the previous verse and says: here is the pit he dug, which from the start he planned to dig for someone else — his punishment is that he himself falls into it.
His mischief will recoil. The harm he wanted to do to another will come back upon his head.
Upon his skull. The idea is repeated in other words, to show that it will always be so.
For His righteousness. As it is fitting to give thanks for the justice of His judgment.
And sing a hymn. I will praise the name of the L-rd in song, saying that He is still higher, far above all praises.
How majestic is Your name. How very mighty You are throughout the earth, watching over all and ruling over all.
You who have covered. For the splendor of Your Shechinah is set in the heavens above; even a weak one above counts as strong — all the more a mighty one above.

From the mouths of infants and sucklings. From the mouths of infants, which are closed in their mothers’ wombs, and when they are born their mouths open and they nurse constantly at their mothers’ breasts: from this wonder You laid a firm foundation for knowing Your strength, for it is something nature does not require.
On account of Your foes. To refute Your foes, who denied the L-rd.
To put an end. To silence the words of the enemy and of the one who takes revenge on those who believe in the L-rd.

When I behold. From this wonder I see with wisdom that Your heavens are the work of Your fingers, and the moon and stars that You set in place are all the work of Your hands, and the world did not always exist.
What is man. He goes on to show that the L-rd watches over everything, and says: what is the worth of man, that he should be remembered before the L-rd?

You have made him little less. With all this, in Your watching over him You made him only a little less than the angels in wisdom and knowledge, and crowned him with glory and majesty, for he rises above every living thing by the gift of speech.
You have made him master. You made him rule over all creatures.
At his feet. That is, they submit to him.
The birds of the heavens. They fly high in the air of the heavens, and still man rules over them and catches them by wisdom.
Whatever travels the paths of the seas. That is, by his wisdom man builds ships, travels the paths of the seas in them, and can catch even the fish of the sea.
How majestic. From all this one sees how majestic is Your name throughout the earth, watching over all and ruling over all.
Singing a hymn to Your name, O Most High. I will praise Him, saying that His name is still higher, exalted above all praises.
When my enemies retreat. When my enemies cannot prevail against me, and turn back, stumble and perish — then I will rejoice and exult: a double joy for a double good.
For You uphold. Many times You have upheld my cause and sat on the throne to judge my enemies.
You blast. For my sake You blasted the nations, etc., and blotted out their name, so that they will not be remembered.

The enemy. You, enemy, know that the ruins are finished forever: that is, the ruined places in you will stay so forever and not return to what they were; and the cities torn down for your sin — their memory will be lost. The idea is repeated in other words.
But the L-rd abides forever. For the L-rd lives forever, and so does His rule; if so, who can rebuild what He has torn down?
It is He who judges. Forever He will judge them with justice, uprightness and righteousness, as they deserve.
A haven for the oppressed. For the brokenhearted He will be a haven. And when will He be a haven? When there is a time of trouble in the world.
For You do not abandon. For they will see that You have not abandoned those who seek You.
Who reigns in Zion. Who rests His Shechinah in Zion.
He who requites bloodshed. For He seeks to know about the blood shed, and they are remembered before Him, even though He does not hurry to punish.
You who lift me. You have always lifted me from the gates of death.
In the pit. In the pit they themselves made.
The L-rd has made Himself known. When He works judgment, then He becomes known and famous to all.
The wicked man is snared. When the wicked man falls into the trap he made, then the Omnipresent’s fame will be remembered in the heart forever.
Let them be. Literally “let them return”: because Sheol is prepared for them, it says “return,” like a man returning to his house prepared for him to live in.
Not always. And by this He will repay those who oppress him.
Forever lost. The word “not” serves both halves, as if it said “will not be forever lost.”
Let not men have power. Let Your enemies not grow strong.
In Your presence. That is, at the time of Your anger.
Strike fear. Bring them low, so that they will know that they are forever mortal men, and not almighty.
Stand aloof. As if You stand far away and hide Yourself in a time of trouble.
In his arrogance. Because of his great arrogance he hounds the poor man and catches him with the scheme he devised to catch him.

The wicked crows. Because the wicked man praises and glorifies himself for getting what he desired, and the robber, while he commits abominations, blesses himself in his heart, saying, “I will have peace,” since nothing was done to him. So people’s hearts are filled with the will to do evil.

Arrogant as he is. When his anger rises high against someone, he thinks that no one will call his deeds to account, and all his thoughts are that there is no G-d in the world to repay him for his deeds.
His ways prosper. Because he succeeds in his ways at all times, and Your judgment is removed from him, and with a little breath he destroys his foes.
He thinks. So he thinks that he will never be shaken or brought down to the ground.
Through all time. Even after many generations he will prosper and see no trouble.
Oaths. He fills his mouth with false oaths and deceit.
Under his tongue. The idea is repeated in other words.
He lurks. The wicked man sits in ambush by the villages, catches the innocent and kills him in secret.
His eyes. He acts as if he turns his eyes away from the poor man, as if he were not thinking of him at all, so that the poor man will not be on guard.

He waits. He waits in a hidden place: like a lion lying in wait in its lair, so he waits to seize the poor man as he pulls. He used the language of a hunter, who pulls the rope of the net to catch whatever comes into it.
He stoops, he crouches. He makes himself look crushed and bent over so that no one notices him, but with his great strength he brings down the poor.
He thinks. All this is because he thinks that either G-d has forgotten his deeds or He does not watch over them.
Rise. Therefore rise and lift Your hand against him to strike him, and do not forget the poor who are caught in his hand.
Why. For what reason did the wicked man's heart dare to scorn G-d? Because he thinks in his heart that You do not call his deeds to account.
You do look. But in truth You have seen his deeds, for You always see the mischief and vexation that the wicked man does.

To requite is in Your power. And it is in Your hand to give a man according to his ways; therefore the poor man gives up his trust in every person and leans on You, for You have always helped the orphan whose help has passed away.
Break. Therefore break the strength of the wicked man, so that he understands that there is a G-d who judges.
And evil man. And then, even one who is used to doing evil — when You look for his wickedness, You will not find it, for he will return to good when he sees that You execute judgment on the wicked.

The L-rd is king, etc. Surely Your kingship is forever, and as Your strength was then, so is Your strength now; surely the nations perished from His land because of their evil deeds. Therefore do so now, too, and destroy the wicked.
The entreaty. Surely You have always listened and fulfilled the desire of the lowly; therefore now, too, when their heart is ready to pray with devotion, listen to them and fulfill their desire.
To champion (lit. “to judge”). To exact judgment for them from their oppressors.
That … no more. And the oppressor will no longer terrify and hurt people, when he sees that You surely repay.

To me (lit. “to my soul”). How can you say about me, “Your mountain wanders like a bird” — that is, the king of Israel wanders, fleeing from Saul, like this wandering bird that in the end falls into a net; so too he will in the end fall into Saul's hand. And he said: How can you say so? Surely I take refuge in the L-rd, and He can do everything and will save me.

For see. That is, if you think that the L-rd has abandoned me because of the sin of the killing of the priests of Nob — surely, see, the wicked bent the bow, etc. This is a parable for the slander that Doeg told Saul about the priests of Nob.
To shoot. The arrows.
From the shadows. That is, in secret.
At the upright. At the priests of Nob.

When the foundations. These wicked men destroyed the foundation of the world — the priests of Nob, righteous men, the foundations of the world. “What has the righteous man done” — David said about himself: Surely I am righteous in this; what have I done? Surely I did nothing.

The L-rd is in His palace, etc. Although the L-rd sits on high in His holy palace in heaven, nevertheless He lowers His eyes to look upon the earth, to test the deeds of mankind, and He knows on whose account this trouble came.

Seeks out the righteous man. That I am pursued by Saul is not because of sin; rather, this is the L-rd's way — to test the righteous man with suffering, whether he will stand firm in his righteousness, in order to make his end good; He does not chastise him out of hatred.
But the wicked one. But He hates the wicked one, even though he is spared suffering.
He will rain down. For in the end he will receive his full recompense: many snares will come down upon him from heaven like rain, and he will be caught in them.
Their lot (lit. “the portion of their cup”). The portion that fills their cup will be of a scorching wind; that is, He will bring great calamities upon them.
Righteous deeds. He loves a man of righteous deeds and will not abandon him into the hand of his enemies.
The upright. The upright man will see the face of the L-rd. This is a parable taken from a king: the one he loves is among those who see his face.
Help, O L-rd. To be saved from Saul's hand.
For the faithful are no more. The faithful man has vanished from the world, and no one can be found to restrain Saul's hand and to plead my case before him.
Have vanished. Men of faithfulness are gone, and they speak lies about me before Saul.
Men speak lies, etc. What they speak softly is a lie, for it is not so in their thoughts.
They talk with duplicity (lit. “with a heart and a heart”). As if the tongue speaks on behalf of one heart, while the other heart does not agree with it.
May the L-rd cut off. He prays that the L-rd cut off the one with flattering lips and the tongue that speaks important and precious words in order to deceive.

By our tongues. Which speak arrogance — we shall prevail over everyone, for we can deceive them. “Lips such as ours” (lit. “our lips are with us”): surely our lips are in our power, and we can speak lies with them, the opposite of what is in the heart; for who is master over us to command us to speak only what is in the heart? Surely, who knows what is in the heart?
Because of the plunder. Because of the plunder that they do to the poor by their cunning.
The groans. Of those who cry out over the plunder. I will act (lit. “I will rise”). To exact payment from them.

“I will give help,” He affirms to him (lit. “he blows at him”). As if it said, “I will give help to the one he blows at”; that is, I will save the one whom the wicked man comes to destroy with a mere breath.

The words of the L-rd. Surely the words of the L-rd are pure like silver that is refined many times in an open place in the depth of the earth, for then it is pure, without dross. So too, nothing of the L-rd's words falls to the ground, for so it will be: He will give strength to the one who destroys the wicked.
Will keep them. The needy.
Guarding each. You will guard each one forever from the hands of the people of that generation.
On every side. For the wicked go around the needy man to catch him, like the gluttonous wild ox that goes around to tear people apart; therefore the needy man has no protection except through You.
How long. Until when will I wander and be driven about? Will You forget me forever?
Have cares (lit. “set counsels”). I will devise plans for how to escape from the grief that is in my heart all day.
Look. See my affliction and answer me.
Restore the luster to my eyes. So that I may find a useful plan to be saved from the enemy's hand, lest I be caught in his hand and sleep the sleep of death, for he would destroy my life.
Lest my enemy say. If not for my sake, then do it lest the enemy say, “I have overcome him, my hand is raised high,” and my foes rejoice when I am about to fall to the ground.
But I. Always, when I trusted in Your faithfulness, my heart rejoiced in the deliverance that came from You.
I will sing. Now, too, I will sing to the L-rd when He bestows His kindness on me.
The benighted man thinks. Nebuzaradan, who destroyed the Holy Temple, said in his heart, “There is no G-d; everything happens by chance.”
Corrupt. He and his people. He said it all in the past tense, for in the prophetic vision he sees it as if it had already been done.
Loathsome deeds. They did abominable deeds, and there is no one among them who does good.
Looks down. To see the deeds of that people.
To find a man of understanding. To protest against it.
Mindful. One who seeks and searches for G-d, that is, who knows that there is a G-d who judges.
All have turned bad. All of them turned away from the good path.
Altogether. All of them together corrupted their deeds.
Are they so witless. That is, how can they say, “There is no G-d”? Surely the evildoers should know that their devouring my people as one eats bread is because my people did not call upon the L-rd.

There. For surely there, in Jerusalem itself, when Sennacherib came against it, they were seized with fright, for they fell as corpses. And our Sages, of blessed memory, said that Nebuchadnezzar himself was with them and was among those who survived.

For G-d. That fright came because the L-rd was with that generation, for it was a righteous generation. But in the days of Nebuchadnezzar they were wicked — and why did the L-rd not help them? But nothing happens by chance.
The counsel of the lowly. You put to shame the counsel of a lowly people, who say in their counsel that the L-rd is their refuge, for you deny it, saying, “There is no G-d.”
O that. If only the deliverance of Israel would come soon from the One who dwells in Zion.
When the L-rd restores. When the L-rd gives rest to those who return, that is, when it is clear to all that the L-rd has given them rest.
Will exult. Then they will rejoice that their counsel — to take refuge in the L-rd — has succeeded, and others will have to admit it to them.

Who may sojourn. As if he asks: “You, L-rd — who is worthy to dwell in Your tent,” that is, the Holy Temple? For not all are worthy, as it is said (Isaiah 1:12): “Who asked, etc., to trample My courts?”
He who lives without blame. As if he answers: the one who walks in a blameless way, etc. — he is the one who will dwell there.
In his heart. What he resolves in his heart regarding a mitzvah, he confirms by doing it.
Borne reproach. He has not cast anything shameful on his neighbor.
A contemptible man. A contemptible person is abhorrent in his eyes, and he flatters no one.
To his hurt. To afflict himself.
Against the innocent. To pervert the judgment of the innocent.
Shall never be shaken. He will not come close to falling, for he does good, and so he is worthy to dwell in the Holy Temple, for the L-rd desires him.
